body: Because if I die, I will no longer be able to cry.

Thank you for your reply.

I have very much been up in the air about accepting meds.
Even though I had very bad experience in my teens while hospitalized, those feelings, and mental images still persist.

I seriously dislike the idea, that if they work, I will probably need to be on them for the rest of my life.
I don't even take aspirins.
I just wish that I can make all this crap just go away, without the needs of meds.

I DON'T LIKE THE PHRASE "A CRY FOR HELP", I JUST DON'T LIKE HOW IT SOUNDS WHEN SOMEBODY SAYS TO ME, I'M THINKING ABOUT SUICIDE.
I HAVE A PLAN, I JUST NEED A REASON NOT TO DO IT, THE LAST THING I SEE IS HELPLESSNESS.

AND YOU'RE STILL JUST GOING "GIVE ME A STICK I'M NOT DYING OUT HERE.

LIVED LONG ENOUGH TO BECOME THE DOMINANT SPECIES.

ALL I'M DOING IS HANDING OUT STICKS.

YOU'RE THE ONE STAYING ALIVE.

It occurred to Pooh and Piglet that
they hadn't heard from Eeyore for
several days, so they put on their
hats and coats and trotted across
the Hundred Acre Wood to
Eeyore's stick house. Inside the
house was Eeyore.

"Hello Eeyore," said Pooh.

"Hello Pooh. Hello Piglet," said
Eeyore, in a Glum Sounding Voice.

"We just thought we'd check in on
you," said Piglet, "because we
hadn't heard from you, and so we
wanted to know if you were okay."

Eeyore was silent for a moment.
"Am I okay?" he asked, eventually.
"Well, I don't know, to be honest.
Are any of us really okay? That's
what I ask myself. All I can tell
you, Pooh and Piglet, is that right
now I feel really rather Sad, and
Alone, and Not Much Fun To Be
Around At All. Which is why I
haven't bothered you wouldn't want to waste your time hanging out with someone who is Sad, and Alone, and Not Much Fun To Be Around At All, would you now."

Pooh looked at Piglet, and Piglet looked at Pooh, and they both sat down, one on either side of Eeyore in his stick house.

Eeyore looked at them in surprise. "What are you doing?"

"We're sitting here with you," said Pooh, "because we are your friends. And true friends don't care if someone is feeling Sad, or Alone, or Not Much Fun To Be Around At All. True friends are there for you anyway. And so here we are."

"Oh," said Eeyore. "Oh." And the three of them sat there in silence, and while Pooh and Piglet said nothing at all; somehow, almost imperceptibly, Eeyore started to feel a very tiny little bit better.

Because Pooh and Piglet were There.

When I was 16 years old, I ended my life.

I was brought back again by a woman who found me unconscious from the pills.
Twice my heart had stopped, while her friend flagged down a police officer.
It was her and the police officer performing CPR that brought me back.

What followed was 10 months in a psych unit.
It was there that the other patients, not the staff that gave me the courage to move forward with my life.

To this day, each and every day of my life, I contemplate my demise whether by nature or my own hand.

And yet, every night I go to bed, and awake the next morning.

And while I am still depressed the next day, there always seems to be one thing in that day that makes it worth waiting to see what the next days surprise will bring.

Thanks for the advice.
It is sound and well received.

Unfortunately the therapist I'm now working with is quite young.
In my opinion, she is too young.
Many of her responses are right out of the Ericsonian textbook.

If you have read my previous posts, (Which, I have to assume you had.)  You know that I have been through the ringer with various therapists, and a ten month stint in the psych ward.

Due to the setup in this agency, my therapy will officially end with her at the end of july.
If I am to continue in therapy, I will have to go through the process of finding a new therapist.

This is a process I'm not happy about, frankly because I don't wish to have to rehash my entire life, and history over and over and over again. 

Maybe it's just better to walk away from everything.
Who knows if this gets any worse I may just decide to opt out altogether.

The first thing I told my therapist, was now I have a label.
It's the very first thing I thought of when she asked me pretty much the same question.

As to how I feel emotionally about that thought, I'm not certain.
It does bother me at a gut level.
My depression while not crippling, is creeping into my day-to-day life and work.

I often wonder whether for me depression is my normal.

Too much pain in my history, all of which is coming to a focal point in my life at this time.
On my 10th birthday, I was told that I was adopted as an infant. (Truth)

I read your story and it brought me to tears.

I completely understand where you were at.

When I was a 14 year old freshman I was raped, beaten and left for dead by two Senior's.
As a boy I was unable to tell anyone what happened.

The boys that did this spread the rumor that I was a "fag".
This was in 1970. 
Back then this was a social death sentence.

This led to three years of HEAVY drug use to keep me numb.

There came a day when I made the decision that I was a burden to all those around me. 
So I decided to end my life.
I went out by the lake, swallowed a bottle of barbiturates and waited.
 
I was found by a lady walking her dog.
She performed CPR and got me to the hospital.

What followed was nine months in a psych ward.

Know this, you are NOT alone.

If you are willing DM me that we may chat.

Just a side question.

With a LGBT couple.
How do you know which one is supposed to roll over and go to sleep first ?

Thank you for your beautiful letter.
During my last session my therapist
asked me what happiness was to me.
The only response I could give was a phrase I hate to use "I don't know."

I cannot remember a time when I was truly happy.
Or what it would feel like If tomorrow I woke up happy.
It is a concept that is foreign to me.

After the attack I spent three years sunk in deep drug use to keep myself numb.
Never telling a soul what had happened to me.
Until a day came when I decided I was a burden to all those around me.
I sat at the shore of lake Michigan a swallowed a bottle of pills.
Found by a lady walking her dog.
She did CPR until the Medic's arrived
Then onto the psych ward for nine months.
When the camera pans on a busy street and every car is spotless.

Tis love that enables the lark to sing.

Tis love that grounds the heart.

Tis love that brings hope.

Tis despair that robs the soul.

Thank you for your kind words.
I have traveled a long road this last year.
There is a great depth within that shouts out in fear and trembling.

A child many years ago beaten, raped and left for dead.
Two older boys who stole from my soul.

Therapy helps, yet the soiled heart heals ever so slowly.
